tag: Coffee estates, waterfalls and the Kodava way of life
ab: Coorg is a misty district of coffee and pepper estates in the Western Ghats, with waterfalls, the source of the Kaveri and a large Tibetan settlement at Bylakuppe.
ppl: The Kodavas are a proud warrior community who are allowed to carry guns without a licence. Weddings feature men in black kupya robes with silver daggers, and families live on ancestral ainmane estates. Pandi curry (pork) with kadambuttu rice balls is the taste of every celebration.

places.d: A waterfall tumbling through coffee and spice plantations, fullest after the monsoon.
The garden where Kodagu's kings watched the sun set over misty hills.
A dazzling monastery with three 18 m golden Buddhas in India's second-largest Tibetan settlement.
A bumpy jeep ride to grassy peaks above the clouds.
The source of the Kaveri river, a spring temple high on Brahmagiri hill.
Learn bean to cup on a Kodava family estate, with pepper vines and orange trees.
A forest-department elephant camp on the river; watch the mahouts at work from the bank.
A 17th-century fort with a small museum and old church.

tag: A royal city of palaces, silk and sandalwood
ab: Mysuru was the capital of the Wodeyar kings. Its palace lights up with 97,000 bulbs, its Dasara is India's grandest royal festival, and its silk, sandalwood and yoga are famous worldwide.
ppl: During Dasara, the city relives its royal past with a procession of decorated elephants carrying the goddess in a golden howdah. Families make Mysore pak at home, the silk weavers' factory still makes sarees for the whole state, and Ashtanga yoga students from around the world live here for months.

places.d: An Indo-Saracenic palace of stained glass, carved doors and a golden throne.
On Sundays and holidays the whole palace lights up with nearly 100,000 bulbs.
The hilltop temple of the city's guardian goddess and a giant stone Nandi on the way up.
Pyramids of coloured kumkum, jasmine garlands and bananas in a 19th-century market.
Terraced gardens below the KRS dam with an evening musical fountain.
Tipu Sultan's island capital: his summer palace, fort walls and the Ranganatha temple.
Boat rides past nesting painted storks, pelicans and basking crocodiles.
A perfect star-shaped Hoysala temple of finely carved soapstone.

tag: The ruined capital of an empire among giant boulders
ab: Hampi was Vijayanagara, one of the world's richest cities in 1500. Its temples, bazaars and palaces lie scattered across a surreal landscape of boulders and banana fields along the Tungabhadra.
ppl: Villagers live inside the ruins: Hampi Bazaar's families run guesthouses in the old pavilions, and coracle men paddle round baskets across the river as they have for centuries. Lakshmi, the temple elephant, once blessed visitors at Virupaksha. Sunrise and sunset from the hills are a daily gathering.
go: Hosapete station 13 km; Hubballi airport 150 km

places.d: A living temple since the 7th century, with a pinhole camera image of the gopuram inside.
The stone chariot on the ₹50 note and pillars that ring like music when tapped.
Small temples on a rocky hill where everyone gathers for sunset.
The Mahanavami platform where kings watched festivals, and a perfect geometric tank.
An airy pavilion for the queens and domed stables for eleven royal elephants.
Spin downriver in a round basket boat past ruined shrines in the rocks.
An older capital across the river with village life, banana-fibre crafts and Hanuman's hill.
The highest point in Hampi, where sunrise lights the boulder fields gold.

tag: A temple town with secret beaches over the cliffs
ab: Gokarna is an ancient Shiva pilgrimage town with a string of beautiful beaches linked by cliff trails: Kudle, Om, Half Moon and Paradise.
ppl: Gokarna's Havyaka Brahmin families have served the Mahabaleshwar temple for generations; their homes have red-tiled roofs and inner courtyards. On the beaches, fishing families run shacks and boat rides, and the town still closes early.
go: Gokarna Road station; Goa airport 140 km

places.d: Two curved bays forming the Om symbol, with water sports and cafés.
A relaxed beach below the cliffs, with shacks and sunset yoga.
A cliff trail to hidden beaches reachable only on foot or by boat.
The Atmalinga temple, one of India's holiest Shiva shrines; men enter bare-chested.
A moss-covered laterite fort with moats and wells, wonderful after the rains.
Two giant black limestone pinnacles in the forest, with caves and a temple.

tag: Where coffee came to India, and Hoysala temples nearby
ab: Chikkamagaluru is where Baba Budan planted India's first coffee beans in the 1600s. Karnataka's highest peaks, waterfalls and the Hoysala temples of Belur and Halebidu are around it.
ppl: Coffee estates here are family affairs, where three generations live in bungalows among the bushes and workers pick ripe red cherries in winter. The Baba Budangiri shrine is honoured by both Hindus and Muslims, a shared tradition centuries old.
go: Kadur station 40 km; Mangaluru airport 150 km

places.d: Karnataka's highest peak (1,930 m), a short climb from the road to a small temple.
A hill shrine revered by Hindus and Muslims, where coffee first came to India.
A 12th-century Hoysala temple with bracket figures of dancers carved like jewellery.
Twin temples whose outer walls carry thousands of friezes of elephants, lions and epics.
A jeep ride through coffee estates to a 168 m waterfall.
Walk the estate with a planter and taste fresh-roasted coffee.

tag: The garden city of tech, breweries and old palaces
ab: Bengaluru is India's tech capital with a mild climate, great gardens, a Tudor-style palace, Tipu Sultan's summer palace and the country's craft-beer scene.
ppl: Old Bengaluru families still start the day at darshinis, standing cafés for idli and filter coffee, and in Basavanagudi the Kadalekai Parishe peanut fair has run for centuries. Young people from every state work here, and the city is famous for its pubs, gigs and weekend escapes to the hills.
go: Kempegowda International Airport; KSR Bengaluru station

places.d: A 240-acre garden with a Victorian glasshouse and a 3,000-million-year-old rock outcrop.
A green heart of rain trees around the red Attara Kacheri and State Library.
A Tudor-style palace modelled on Windsor Castle.
A teak palace with painted arches, near the old Kote Venkataramana temple.
A lane of vegetarian street food: holige, dosa, gulkand and more.
A hill fort above the clouds an hour from the city.
Lion and tiger safaris and a butterfly park on the city's edge.
Indiranagar's microbreweries, India's craft-beer capital.

tag: City of Nizams, pearls and the best biryani in India
ab: Hyderabad was the capital of the Qutb Shahi kings and the Nizams, once the world's richest men. Charminar, Golconda fort and the old city's bazaars sit beside a modern tech city.
ppl: Hyderabadis mix Telugu and Urdu into their own Dakhni speech ('hau', 'nakko'). The old city's chai is Irani, served with Osmania biscuits, and Ramzan nights bring haleem cooked for hours in giant pots. Laad Bazaar's bangle makers have worked lac and stones for 400 years.
fest: Ramzan nights in the old city
go: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport; Secunderabad and Hyderabad stations

places.d: The four-minaret arch of 1591, surrounded by a bazaar of glittering lac bangles.
The Nizams' palace of chandeliers, vintage cars and a durbar hall.
The diamond-trading fortress where a handclap at the gate can be heard at the top.
Domed tombs of the Golconda kings in a beautifully restored park.
One man's collection of 40,000 objects, including the veiled Rebecca and a musical clock.
A boat ride to a monolithic Buddha in the middle of the lake at sunset.
Irani chai at Nimrah, biryani and kebabs as the old city comes alive at night.
The world's largest film studio complex with sets, shows and rides.

tag: The world's most visited temple on seven hills
ab: Tirumala's Sri Venkateswara temple, on the seven hills above Tirupati, is one of the world's richest and busiest pilgrimage sites. Pilgrims walk up the 3,550 steps or take the ghat road.
ppl: Many pilgrims offer their hair to the god as a sign of surrender, so you'll see families with freshly shaved heads everywhere. The famous Tirupati laddu is made in a temple kitchen that turns out lakhs a day, and devotees walk the Alipiri steps chanting 'Govinda'.

places.d: Darshan of Lord Venkateswara; the special-entry ticket shortens the wait.
places.t: Book darshan slots on the TTD website weeks ahead.

places.d: 3,550 steps up the hill through forest, the traditional pilgrim route.
The temple of the god's consort; tradition says visit before Tirumala.
A rare natural rock arch 1.5 billion years old near the temple.
A waterfall into a temple tank at the foot of the hills.
A Vijayanagara fort and palace with an evening sound and light show.

tag: Tribal coffee country in the Eastern Ghats
ab: Araku is a high valley of coffee farms, Borra's huge limestone caves and tribal villages, reached by one of India's most scenic railway lines from Visakhapatnam.
ppl: Over a dozen Adivasi communities live here, and the Dhimsa dance, women in a circle moving to drums, welcomes visitors. Araku coffee, now sold in Paris, is grown organically by tribal farmers' cooperatives on small plots.
go: Araku station on the Kirandul line; Visakhapatnam airport 115 km

places.d: Million-year-old limestone caves with stalactites in shapes of gods and animals.
The story of coffee from bean to cup, with handmade chocolates to taste.
Life-size models of tribal homes, hunting and rituals, with Dhimsa dance shows.
One of the highest points in the Eastern Ghats, over coffee and silver-oak forest.
Water tumbling over flat rocks, a favourite local picnic spot.
Walk a smallholder's organic coffee plot and share a cup with the family.

tag: History, coral and the start of island-hopping
ab: Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) is the capital of the Andamans: the Cellular Jail where freedom fighters were imprisoned, colonial ruins on Ross Island and coral reefs at North Bay.
ppl: The Andamans are a mini-India: families from Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Ranchi settled here, and people greet each other with 'Jai Hind'. The islands' first peoples, like the Jarawa and Onge, live in protected reserves that visitors must respect and never photograph.
go: Veer Savarkar International Airport; ships from Chennai and Kolkata

places.d: The 'Kala Pani' prison where freedom fighters were held in solitary cells.
An emotional evening show in the jail courtyard.

places.n: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep)
places.d: The British headquarters, now ruins swallowed by banyan roots, with tame deer and peacocks.
Snorkel or look through a glass floor at coral and fish.
A bird-filled forest point at the south tip with the islands' best sunset.
A palm-lined beach near town with water sports.
Corals, shells and the islands' tribes and history, run by the Navy.

tag: Turquoise water, white sand and the best diving in India
ab: Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) has Radhanagar, one of Asia's finest beaches, and coral reefs for diving. Smaller Neil (Shaheed Dweep) is a quiet island of natural rock bridges and village roads. Ferries link them to Port Blair.
ppl: Bengali settler families, brought here in the 1960s, farm betel nut and paddy and run small guesthouses; the island's villages are simply named by numbers. Life moves at ferry speed, and the whole island goes quiet after 9 PM.

places.d: A long arc of white sand and turquoise water with forest behind, famous for its sunsets.
A boat ride to shallow coral reefs full of parrotfish and clownfish.
A guided first dive among corals with a certified instructor.
A quiet beach edged by black rocks, best at sunrise.
A coral rock arch exposed at low tide, with tide pools of sea life.
A wide, shell-strewn beach for the sunset on Neil.
